THE STORY IS LATENCY, NOT BYTES. Point reads are 1-4 ms; four rollups are 35 of 40 s.

⭐⭐ CAUSE 3 — THE MULTIPLIER, FOUND LAST AND LARGEST: EVERY READ AFTER A WRITE RUNS A FULL loop_status TO APPEND A ONE-LINE HINT. `service.rs:3731 read_loop_hint` computes `g.loop_status()` and caches it keyed on `write_gen`; `write_gen.fetch_add` is at `service.rs:3647` in the single write-lock path, so EVERY write invalidates it and the NEXT read of ANY kind recomputes. Measured on a scratch copy, alternating create_node / get_node: reads after a write cost 7,672 / 7,770 / 6,719 ms; the writes themselves 82-127 ms; the second read 1-2 ms. TEN CALLS, 30.3 s, 29.9 s OF IT HIDDEN loop_status. Server log is silent throughout (no tantivy, no rocksdb) — it is reflow2's own rollup. On the live shared daemon, where loop_status is 12.5 s, the same mechanism costs ~12 s per write→read transition (inferred from the measured parts, not separately timed). A ~164-call session with writes interleaved pays this dozens of times: MINUTES of unrequested rollup per session, decorating 452-byte reads. `describe_schema` (no store) cold 6 ms and `claim_report` (no hint) show no spike — the subtraction that located it.

⭐ CAUSE 1 — WHAT THAT HIDDEN loop_status IS MADE OF: `open_defects()` UNCACHED. 5.2-5.8 s per run, `heal.rs:964`, no memoisation, TEN call sites; three are orientation rollups (`report.rs:853 loop_status_for`, `:1348 graph_report`, `:597 debt_since` — so `since_export: true` pays twice). Computed to produce a COUNT.

⭐ CAUSE 2 — FIVE DEAD SCRATCH EXPORTS COST EVERY loop_status ~3.5 s. `sync_status` alone: 3,556 ms live (6 targets) vs 19 ms fresh (0). 53.7 MB parsed per call; five are one-off `/tmp` files from dead sessions. The SAME five whose false claims v0.47.1 fixed — the claim went, the read stayed.

TOGETHER: a write→read transition on the live daemon = open_defects 5.8 + sync 3.6 + detect_gaps 1.8 + other ≈ 12 s, paid for a hint.

🛑 FOUR HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED, so nobody re-tests them: (a) STORE BLOAT — live 104 MB / 22 SST vs fresh 17 MB / 0 SST for identical content; every rollup within noise on the fresh store. (b) GRAPH GROWTH — v0.46.0 design (3% smaller) costs the same. (c) `rehydrate_gaps` PER GAP — `ask.rs:381` runs detect_gaps once. (d) CODE REGRESSION SINCE v0.46.0 — a v0.46.0 release binary on a store it wrote: open_questions 8,906, loop_status 6,857, detect_defects 5,053 — indistinguishable from 0.47.1 on the same design. The recorded 2.95 s for open_questions was taken under conditions not reproduced here.

⚠️ TWO NEAR-MISSES KEPT: the v0.46.0 binary first refused a 0.47.1-written store with `-32602 tool not found` in 0.2 ms — without the profiler's ERR column that reads as a 10,000x win (`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object`); and a 40-line cap on a log read hid the lines that mattered until re-pulled uncapped.

⚠️ STILL UNEXPLAINED: open_questions ~7 s over 57 Questions (~123 ms each) beyond detect_gaps; needs a timing probe inside `detect.rs:1765`. ALSO OBSERVED, UNINVESTIGATED: tantivy runs a COMMIT and GARBAGE-COLLECT on every read-only open (~300 ms, deleting segment files) — every session start mutates the index directory.

📌 BOUNDS. One machine, 4 cores, desktop load floor ~2, release, stdio.
